questions.question: Which of the following scenarios is an example of an object possessing energy?

options.B: A book lying on a table

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): A compressed spring. Spring → elastic potential energy; Book → gravitational potential energy.

questions.question: When a ball is thrown straight up into the air, at the highest point:

options.A: Kinetic energy is maximum, potential energy is zero
options.B: Kinetic energy is zero, potential energy is maximum
options.C: Both kinetic and potential energy are equal

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Kinetic energy is maximum, potential energy is zero. Velocity = 0 → K.E = 0; height maximum → P.E = maximum.

questions.question: During photosynthesis, plants convert:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Kinetic energy into chemical energy. Sunlight → chemical energy in glucose.

questions.question: Hydroelectric energy is generated by converting which types of energy into electrical energy?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Potential. Water’s gravitational potential energy → kinetic → electrical.

questions.question: Which of the following is a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Natural gas. Renewable energy naturally replenishes.

questions.question: One disadvantage of solar power compared to fossil fuels is that solar power:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Is not always available. Solar depends on sunlight; not available at night/cloudy days.

questions.question: A box is dragged across a floor with a constant force. If the force is doubled and the distance remains the same, how does the work done change?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): It doubles. Work = Force × Distance. Doubling force doubles work.

questions.question: The energy stored within the nucleus of an atom is known as:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Nuclear energy. Nuclear energy is released in fission or fusion.

questions.question: Which of the following energy sources is considered non-renewable?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Coal. Coal is finite; non-renewable.

questions.question: Which of the following is a renewable resource that relies on the cycle of water?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Tidal energy. Tidal energy depends on moon-sun gravitational cycles.

questions.question: A person lifts boxes of equal weight onto a platform. Which quantity will not affect the work done by the person?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Time taken. Work = Force × Distance; time does not affect work.

questions.question: One kilo joule is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 1000 J. "Kilo" means 1000. So, 1 kJ = 1000 J.

questions.question: The work will be maximum when the angle between force and displacement is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 0°. Work = F × d × cos(θ). Maximum when cos(θ) = 1 → θ = 0°.

questions.question: Capability to do work of a body is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Energy. Energy is defined as the capacity to do work.

questions.question: Energy stored in a Dam’s water is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Potential Energy. Water at height has gravitational potential energy: GPE = m × g × h.

questions.question: In Einstein’s mass-energy equation, “c” is the:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Speed of light. E = mc², where c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s, the speed of light.

questions.question: 10 Joule work is done by machine in 5 seconds. Its power will be:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 10 W. Power = Work / Time = 10 / 5 = 2 W.

questions.question: One mega joule is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 10⁶ J. “Mega” means 10⁶, so 1 MJ = 10⁶ J.

questions.question: SI unit of work is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Joule. Work = Force × Distance; SI unit is Joule (1 J = 1 N × 1 m).

questions.question: Hammer raised up has energy:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Sound Energy. Hammer has gravitational potential energy = m × g × h.

questions.question: There is a hot molten part deep in the Earth called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Magma. Magma is molten rock beneath the Earth’s surface; lava is magma that reaches the surface.

questions.question: Rate of doing work is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Power. Power = Work / Time.

questions.question: The work will be zero when the angle between the force and displacement is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 90°. Work = F × d × cos(θ). Cos(90°) = 0 → Work = 0.

questions.question: One Joule is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 1 m × 1 N. 1 Joule is work done by 1 Newton force moving an object 1 meter.

questions.question: Kinetic energy is directly proportional to the velocity of a body:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Square. K.E = 1/2 m v² → proportional to the square of velocity.

questions.question: The energy stored in coal is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Chemical Energy. Burning coal releases chemical energy stored in the bonds of molecules.

questions.question: The efficiency of solar cell is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 12%. Typical solar cell converts ~12% of sunlight into electricity.

questions.question: One horse power is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 746 W. Standard conversion: 1 HP = 746 Watts.

questions.question: The work done lifting a brick of mass 2 kg through a height of 5 m above the ground will be:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 100 J. W = m × g × h = 2 × 10 × 5 = 100 J.

questions.question: The energy in the stretched bow is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Elastic Potential Energy. Stretching a bow stores energy in elastic form.

questions.question: The device converts light energy into electrical energy:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Photocell. Photocell uses photoelectric effect to convert light → electricity.

questions.question: The efficiency percentage of an electric lamp is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 5%. Most electrical energy converts to heat; visible light ~5%.

questions.question: One mega-watt is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 10⁶ W. “Mega” = 10⁶; 1 MW = 10⁶ W.

questions.question: The SI unit of energy is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Joule. Energy measured in Joules.

questions.question: The formula of K.E is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 1/2 mv². K.E = 1/2 × mass × velocity².

questions.question: The major source of heat energy is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): The earth. Sun is the primary source of energy for Earth.

questions.question: For maintaining the body temperature energy is used:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Heat. Heat energy helps maintain constant body temperature.

questions.question: For the propagation of signals in our body energy is used:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Electrical. Nerve impulses require electrical energy.

questions.question: A bowler during playing cricket throws a ball of mass 200 g with 20 m/s velocity. Its K.E is:
For work, conditions should be fulfilled:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 1. The Two Conditions for Work 1)Force must be applied: An external force (F) must act upon the object. 2) Displacement must occur: The object must move a certain distance (d) in the direction of the force (or have a component of motion along the line of action of the force).

questions.question: Which unit is equal to kg·m²/s² in the units given below?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Joule. 1 Joule = 1 N·m = 1 kg·m²/s².

questions.question: How much power is used by a 40 kg athlete by climbing 10 m high ladder in 10 s?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 400 W. Work = m × g × h = 40 × 10 × 10 = 4000 J; Power = 4000 / 10 = 400 W.

questions.question: When a spring is compressed, it possesses:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Elastic potential. Compressed spring stores energy in elastic form.

questions.question: If a person exerts force which causes a car to move forward, then this is an example of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Work done. Force × displacement along force = work done.

questions.question: The potential energy of a freely falling body:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Decreases. As the body falls, height decreases → P.E decreases.

questions.question: The product of force and moment arm is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Work. Force × moment arm = Torque, not work.

questions.question: Work done will be if no force acts on the body:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Zero. No force → Work = F × d × cos(θ) = 0.

questions.question: What is the kinetic energy of a pendulum when it reaches at the maximum position?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Maximum. At maximum height, velocity = 0 → K.E = 0.

questions.question: When the force and displacement are in the opposite direction then the work is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Negative. Work = F × d × cos(θ); cos(180°) = -1 → Work negative.

questions.question: The efficiency percentage of an electric motor is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 80%. Practical electric motors typically have ~80% efficiency.

questions.question: The useful work done by an electric fan is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 80 J. Standard Input: 100 J (Total Electrical Energy). Efficiency: 80%= 80/100=0.80 Useful work= Efficiency x total input energy Calculation: Useful work= 0.80 x 100J= 80J In this scenario, 80 J is the useful work (kinetic energy for moving air), while the remaining 20 J is wasted as heat and sound.

questions.question: If the kinetic energy of a 200 Kg object is 10,000 J, then the velocity of object will be:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 10 m/s. K.E = 1/2 m v² → 10,000 = 1/2 × 200 × v² → v² = 100 → v = 10 m/s.

questions.question: A car travels 150 m distance in the direction of a constant force of 50 N. The work done on the car is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 7500 J. Work = F × d = 50 × 150 = 7500 J.

questions.question: kWh is a unit for:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Energy. kWh = 1000 W × 1 hour; measures energy consumed.

questions.question: The potential energy of the system in the state of unstable equilibrium is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Maximum. Unstable equilibrium → small displacement decreases P.E → P.E at maximum.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a unit of energy?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Watt. Watt is a unit of power, not energy.

questions.question: Work is said to be done when:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'A force causes displacement'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: If displacement is zero, work done is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Zero'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: A coolie carries a load on his head and walks on a horizontal path. Work done by him is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Zero'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Positive work is done when:

options.A: Force and displacement are in same direction

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Force and displacement are in same direction'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Negative work is done when:

options.A: Force and displacement are in opposite directions

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Force and displacement are in opposite directions'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: SI unit of energy is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Joule'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Energy possessed by a body due to motion is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Kinetic Energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Potential energy is due to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Position or configuration'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Formula for kinetic energy:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): '½ mv²'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: If the speed of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Four times'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Formula for potential energy:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'mgh'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Unit of power is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Watt'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Power is defined as:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Rate of doing work'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: A man lifts a 10 kg object to a height of 2 m. Work done =
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): '196 J'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition. Reference key: (Using W = mgh = 10 × 9.8 × 2 = 196 J).

questions.question: Horsepower is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): '746 watts'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: A body is lifted vertically upward. The work done is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Positive'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: If force is perpendicular to displacement, work done is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Zero'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: What type of quantity is work?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Scalar'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: If a machine does 500 J of work in 10 seconds, its power is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): '50 W'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Which one is a form of mechanical energy?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Potential energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Energy stored in food is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Chemical energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Solar energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The main disadvantage of fossil fuels is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Causes pollution'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The ultimate source of energy on Earth is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Sun'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Unit of energy used by electric companies is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Kilowatt-hour'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Energy cannot be created or destroyed is the law of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Conservation of Energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: A 60 W bulb uses how much energy in 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): '0.12 kWh'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition. Reference key: (Energy = Power × Time = 60 W × 2 h = 120 Wh = 0.12 kWh).

questions.question: When a ball is at the highest point during free fall, it has:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Maximum potential energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Energy due to position is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Potential energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Work-energy principle states:

options.C: Work done = Change in kinetic energy

questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Work done = Change in kinetic energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Kinetic energy depends on:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Mass and velocity'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: A pendulum at its lowest position has:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Maximum kinetic energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: A fuel with high energy output per unit mass is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Gasoline'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Efficiency is the ratio of:

options.B: Useful output energy to input energy

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Useful output energy to input energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The efficiency of an ideal machine is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): '100%'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 6 (Work & Energy), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.
